'''Ballspielverein Borussia 09 e. V. Dortmund''', often known simply as '''Borussia Dortmund''' ({{IPA|de|boˈʁʊsi̯a ˈdɔʁtmʊnt|-|De-Borussia Dortmund.ogg}}){{Citation |last=Mangold |first=Max|year=2005 |title=Das Aussprachewörterbuch|publisher=Duden |isbn=978-3-411-04066-7|pages=212 and 282}} or by its initialism '''BVB''' ({{IPA|de|ˌbeːfaʊ̯ˈbeː|pron|De-BVB.ogg}}), or just '''Dortmund''' by international fans, is a German professional [[sports club]] based in [[Dortmund]], North Rhine-Westphalia. It is best known for its men's professional [[football club (association football)|football]] team, which plays in the [[Bundesliga]], the top tier of the [[German football league system]]. Founded in 1909 by eighteen football players from Dortmund, they are nicknamed ''Die Schwarzgelben'' (The Black and Yellow), for the colours used in the club's crest.{{cite web |url= http://www.puma.com/football/teams/42-borussia-dortmund |title= Borussia Dortmund – Puma SE |work= puma.com |publisher= [[Puma SE]] |access-date= 17 August 2013 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20140113053901/http://www.puma.com/football/teams/42-borussia-dortmund |archive-date= 13 January 2014 |url-status=dead |df= dmy-all }}{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/nationalassociations/teams/52758--b-dortmund/|title=Borussia Dortmund|publisher=[[UEFA]]|access-date=17 August 2013|archive-date=19 August 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130819004812/http://www.uefa.com/teamsandplayers/teams/club=52758/profile/index.html|url-status=live}} They hold a long-standing rivalry with [[Ruhr]] neighbours [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]], against whom they contest the [[Revierderby]]. They also contest [[Der Klassiker]] with [[FC Bayern Munich]]. Dortmund is the largest sports club by membership in Germany after FC Bayern Munich, with about 218,000 members,{{Cite web |title=Borussia Dortmund: 218.000 Mitglieder – enteilt der BVB nun Schalke? |url=https://www.reviersport.de/fankurve/a/a610763---borussia-dortmund-218-000-mitglieder-enteilt-bvb-nun-schalke.html |access-date=25 November 2024 |website=RevierSport online |language=de}} making Borussia Dortmund the [[List of sports clubs by membership|fifth largest sports club by membership]] in the world. The club also has a [[Borussia Dortmund Handball|women's handball]] team. Since 1974, Dortmund have played their home games at the [[Westfalenstadion]]; the stadium is the largest in Germany, the ''Yellow Wall'', a standing terrace in the South Stand, is the largest of its kind in Europe, and Dortmund has the highest average attendance of any [[Football club (association football)|association football club]] in the world.{{Cite web|url=https://talksport.com/football/525568/top-50-average-football-attendances-in-the-world-in-the-last-five-years-including-manchester-united-barcelona-and-borussia-dortmund/|title=The top 50 average attendances in football over the last five years|date=12 April 2019|access-date=21 February 2020|archive-date=21 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200221065947/https://talksport.com/football/525568/top-50-average-football-attendances-in-the-world-in-the-last-five-years-including-manchester-united-barcelona-and-borussia-dortmund/|url-status=live}} Dortmund is the second most decorated German football team; domestically, they have eight [[List of German football champions|league championships]], five [[DFB-Pokal]]s, and six [[DFL-Supercup]]s. Internationally, they won the [[UEFA Champions League]] in [[1996–97 UEFA Champions League|1997]], the [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup|European Cup Winners' Cup]] in [[1965–66 European Cup Winners' Cup|1966]], and the [[Intercontinental Cup (1960–2004)|Intercontinental Cup]] in [[1997 Intercontinental Cup|1997]], in addition to being the runners-up in the Champions League in [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League|2013]] and [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League|2024]] and in the UEFA Cup (now the [[UEFA Europa League]]) in [[1992–93 UEFA Cup|1993]] and [[2001–02 UEFA Cup|2002]]. Under the directorship of [[Michael Zorc]] in the 2010s, Dortmund cultivated a reputation for spotting and developing young talent, and have remained focused on developing a [[youth system]].{{cite web|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/why-borussia-dortmund-not-so-secret-recipe-for-success-so-hard-to-copy-a4110971.html|title=Why Borussia Dortmund's not-so-secret recipe for success is so hard to copy|date=6 April 2019|publisher=Standard|access-date=3 February 2020|archive-date=3 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200203153130/https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/why-borussia-dortmund-not-so-secret-recipe-for-success-so-hard-to-copy-a4110971.html|url-status=live}} As of 2024, Dortmund had the second most revenue across football clubs in Germany, and the 12th most revenue across all football teams in the world, per [[Deloitte]]'s [[Deloitte Football Money League|Football Money League]].{{cite web| title = Deloitte Football Money League 2024 (rankings for the 2022–23 season)| url = https://www.deloitte.com/uk/en/services/financial-advisory/analysis/deloitte-football-money-league.html| website = www.deloitte.com| access-date = 2 June 2024}}"}}
